Title: Malaysia to expand local currency use through BRICS cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia aims to enhance the use of local currencies in cross-border trade and investment transactions through BRICS cooperation.
In doing so, Malaysia hopes to reduce transaction costs and foreign exchange risks, said the Finance Ministry.
It said the move also aims to strengthen the country's financial resilience against external shocks while providing businesses with more options for conducting international transactions.
It added that wider use of local currencies could improve the efficiency of foreign exchange exposure management and support the development of regional foreign exchange markets.
"An increase in transactions using regional currencies, including those of BRICS member countries, could also enhance liquidity and support the development of regional foreign exchange markets, thereby providing businesses with more options," the ministry said in the Dewan Rakyat.
It was responding to Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang (PN-Marang) on reforms to the international financial system that Malaysia is pursuing through BRICS.
The ministry said Malaysia had also implemented various initiatives with major trading partners, including cooperation with China to facilitate the use of the renminbi and ringgit in bilateral trade.
Malaysia has also implemented the Local Currency Transaction Framework (LCTF) with Indonesia and Thailand.
The ministry said Malaysia would continue to strengthen and improve existing channels and mechanisms to facilitate and expand the use of local currencies in cross-border trade and investment.
However, it noted that the use of major currencies in international trade and finance remained driven by structural factors, including the size of financial markets and their widespread acceptance among businesses and investors.
"Therefore, efforts to expand the use of local currencies must be market-driven, supported by efficient cross-border payment infrastructure and continuous cooperation between countries," it added. — BERNAMA

Title: Malaysia's Global Sukuk attracts US$9.5bil demand, reflecting investor confidence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The issuance of Malaysia's US$1.5 billion Global Sukuk at the end of July 2026 received subscription demand exceeding US$9.5 billion (about RM38.1 billion), reflecting the continued confidence of international investors in the country's economic prospects and credit position.
The Finance Ministry said the issuance of the two tranches of sukuk recorded an oversubscription of 4.7 times, allowing the government to obtain the lowest spread in the history of Malaysia's Global Sukuk issuance.
"The strong demand allowed the government to reduce the spread by 30 basis points (bps) from the initial price guidance for both tranches.
"This resulted in the 5.75-year maturity tranche being priced at 15 bps above the 5-year US Treasury rate of 4.612 per cent per annum, while the 10-year tranche was priced at 25 bps above the 10-year US Treasury rate of 4.949 per cent per annum," it said in a written response published on the Parliament website today.
The ministry noted that the spreads were almost equivalent to the issuance pricing of countries rated A1 and AA2, even though Malaysia has a sovereign credit rating of A3.
"This reflects confidence in Malaysia's credit prospects driven by strong macroeconomic fundamentals and a commitment to fiscal discipline and ongoing structural reforms," the ministry said.
In addition, the government ensures that debt issuance is carried out within the established limits and legal framework.
Following the issuance of the 2026 Global Sukuk, the government's offshore debt stood at RM23 billion, which accounted for only about 1.7 per cent of the total Federal Government debt and remained well below the statutory limit of RM35 billion under the Foreign Loans Act 1963.
This relatively small offshore debt exposure also helps limit currency fluctuations and international market uncertainties, the ministry added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Europe fridge cyberattacks expose weaknesses
Article:
Cyberattacks affecting supermarket refrigeration systems in several European countries on Monday highlighted the risks associated with connecting industrial equipment to the Internet.
After a previous attack in France last month, several chains in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden experienced stark rises in fridge and freezer temperatures on Monday, forcing them to throw away spoilt produce.
Industrial equipment such as refrigeration systems, once operated largely offline, is now commonly connected to the Internet so it can be monitored and managed remotely, said cybersecurity specialists including Antoine Hautin, secretary-general of the Almond cybersecurity consultancy.
That connectivity can also provide an avenue for attackers to interfere with physical systems through digital networks.
In France, the attackers targeted the fridge regulation system made by the Danish firm Danfoss, which is used by many shops.
"Most of the time, that's done through a web interface. You connect to it with a password and you then have the possibility to choose what the temperature in the fridge is," said Kevin Tellier, a cybersecurity engineer at Synacktiv.
While these systems "are normally on a closed network" and "are not supposed to be accessible from the Internet", a number of them ended up being exposed "to anyone with some basic knowledge", he added.
Without proper protections, "any factory or equipment" connected to the Internet—ranging from carmakers to electricity or transport infrastructure —could face similar risks, said Olivier Daloy, a cybersecurity expert at Zscaler.
According to another cyber expert who requested anonymity, industrial infrastructure is particularly vulnerable because it links information technology (IT) systems with oft-outdated physical equipment.
By infiltrating those IT systems, hackers could hijack that infrastructure and cause disruption in the real world.
Daloy highlighted two particular risks: the exploitation of a technical vulnerability and the use of compromised credentials allowing hackers to log in to the equipment.
He pointed to the Stuxnet virus in 2010, which caused a series of failures in Iran's centrifuge fleet used for uranium enrichment, as a past example.
In Belgium, dozens of grocery stores and an Ikea superstore saw their refrigerator temperatures soar on Monday, with several of the firms involved confirming they had been hit by a cyberattack.
Carrefour Belgium reported disruption in about 15 of its 700 stores in Belgium.
"It's a cyberattack, there is no other reason," said Mich Vergauwen, a spokesperson for Carrefour Belgium.
An Ikea Belgium spokesperson likewise said a cyberattack hit its store in Mons, southwestern Belgium, causing the temperature of freezers to rise suddenly in the early hours of Monday.
It is the only Ikea store affected because it uses a different service provider than others in Belgium, the spokesperson added, without identifying the provider.
In France, last month's cyberattack was made possible by "basic security shortcomings", according to Vincent Strubel, head of France's National Cybersecurity Agency.
In particular, he blamed the fridges' "direct exposure to the Internet... without any particular security and with weak passwords".
Figuring out who could be behind the attack in France is "extremely complicated", said Daloy.
Tellier agreed. "It could be anybody. The attack was not extremely sophisticated, so we cannot determine whether the hackers have significant resources or not."
One security source said the investigation into the breach will "extend far after the event itself".
A 2025 French national security document identified such attacks as "one of the threats that must be treated as a priority".
"These incidents highlight how vulnerable food supply chains are to cyberattacks", with far-reaching consequences, said the document.
The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget's most important story isn't in the numbers
Article:
Every year, the ritual is almost familiar. Analysts pore over allocations. Economists scrutinise deficit projections. Politicians argue over winners and losers. Journalists compare this year's figures with last year's. It's usually an annual exercise in accounting.
Yet the most interesting thing about the 2027 Budget may not be a single allocation, tax measure or subsidy adjustment. It's the fact that the document appears to be trying to do something much larger.
For perhaps the first time in years, a Malaysian budget reads less like an accounting exercise and more like a statement of what kind of nation we intend to become. That distinction matters.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also finance minister, connected powerfully when he opened with important references to national unity, volunteerism, the Asian Games, the Formula 1 race at Sepang and the spirit of Segulai Sejalai, one of Sarawak's most cherished slogans for "Advancing together as one".
Those citations seemed detached from the hard business of economics, but in hindsight, they were not.
Anwar appeared to be making a larger argument: that a nation's greatest competitive advantage is ultimately its people, united by a common purpose.
If read carefully, we see a recurring theme: The government is not simply asking how much Malaysia can spend. It's asking what kind of Malaysia we are preparing. That's perhaps the most overlooked aspect of the 2027 Budget.
Anwar's speech repeatedly returns to ideas that traditional economists often regard as peripheral: unity, values, trust, talent, integrity, volunteerism, culture and social cohesion.
Yet these are not presented as decorative themes. They're woven directly into the economic narrative.
The implicit argument is both ambitious and refreshing. A divided society cannot become a high-performing economy. A low-trust society cannot become an innovative society. A nation plagued by cynicism cannot become globally competitive.
In other words, social capital is economic capital. That insight deserves more attention from us Malaysians than we have given it before.
For decades, Malaysians were taught to think of national unity as a social objective and economic growth as a separate economic objective.
But the 2027 Budget quietly suggests they are the same thing.
Equally significant is the budget's emphasis on capability over dependency. Public debate tends to focus on aid, assistance and subsidies. Understandably so. These measures affect daily life.
But beneath the headlines lies another philosophy. The recurring focus on skills, technology, innovation, talent development and productivity suggests a government trying to move the national conversation from welfare to capability.
The message is subtle but clear. The best social protection is not perpetual assistance. It's the ability of citizens to thrive on their own. That's a more difficult agenda. It's also a more transformative one.
Another underappreciated feature of the 2027 Budget is its confidence. For much of the past decade, Malaysia's public discourse has often been dominated by anxiety.
We worried about lost opportunities, declining competitiveness, political instability and brain drain. We became accustomed to managing expectations rather than expanding ambitions.
But this budget does not read like the work of a nation nervously managing decline. It's of a nation attempting to prepare for ascent. The significance lies in the attempt itself.
It was most telling when Anwar quoted the wisdom of the renowned "Shangtang Kaisi" poem by Huangbo Xiyun, a Buddhist monk during the Tang Dynasty (AD 618-907), which reads: "How can the plum blossom release its fragrance without first enduring the bitter cold that penetrates to the bone?"
That metaphor reflected a fundamental truth about life and the human struggle: great achievements do not come from prolonged comfort, but require perseverance, patience and the willingness to endure hardship.
The 2027 Budget is trying to shift Malaysia's mindset from consumption to capability, from assistance to aspiration, from managing today's problems to preparing for tomorrow's possibilities.
The numbers will matter. They always do. But long after the allocations are spent and the headlines forgotten, the 2027 Budget may be remembered for something else entirely.
It's an attempt to rally Malaysians to believe that the future is not something that happens to us, but something we must consciously build together.
Growth, unity, integrity and opportunity are not competing goals, but inseparable pillars of a stronger nation.
The writer is a former Bernama chief executive officer and editor-in-chief
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar moved after being gifted photo of his first parliamentary election victory
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was deeply moved upon receiving an old photograph from a student from Alor Star which captured him celebrating his first electoral victory for the Permatang Pauh parliamentary seat in 1982.
In a Facebook post, the prime minister shared that the photograph was presented by Zahra Mohamad Zelman, who approached him accompanied by her friends from SMK Sultanah Asma at the Parliament building today.
Anwar noted that the image captured a moment when he was being celebrated by Zahra's great-grandfather, the late Arshad Ahmad, following his win in the Permatang Pauh constituency.
"A single photograph, yet it holds so many memories and stories. It evokes a time which has long since passed, but the remembrance of the individuals who were once present who became part of this long journey of struggle remains etched deep within my heart," he wrote in the post.
During the encounter, Anwar encouraged Zahra and her friends to continue their pursuit of knowledge, to have the courage to harbour and pursue their aspirations, and to never cease in their efforts. He also offered prayers that their life journeys would always be made smooth. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Education incentive payments to 2,504 senior teachers to end this month
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Education Incentive Payment Scheme (ETPS) payments to 2,504 senior subject teachers at secondary schools who are no longer eligible following the schools' regrading exercise will be discontinued from this month.
The Education Ministry, in a statement today, also said it would pay outstanding ETPS payments to 1,356 senior subject teachers at secondary schools that have been upgraded to Grade A next year.
It said that for the teachers who are no longer eligible, the ministry would implement adjustments to the ETPS repayment arrangements and ensure the process is managed prudently to avoid placing a financial burden on them.
"The ministry understands the concerns raised by the teachers regarding the ETPS following the school regrading exercise, which came into effect on Jan 11.
"The regrading exercise was carried out based on three criteria, namely student enrolment, the number of hostel residents and the level of education offered.
"Under the revised grading system, secondary schools are now classified as Grade A or Grade B. A total of 339 secondary schools were upgraded from Grade B to Grade A, while 626 secondary schools were downgraded from Grade A to Grade B," the ministry said.
Meanwhile, under the prevailing Public Service Remuneration System regulations, only senior subject teachers at Grade A secondary schools are eligible to receive the ETPS of RM120 per month.
The change in the grading status of secondary schools has directly affected 3,860 serving such teachers.
In this regard, the ministry held several engagement sessions with teachers' unions from March to July this year.
The statement added that during the sessions, the unions proposed submitting an appeal to the Public Service Department to allow Grade B secondary school senior subject teachers to qualify for the ETPS.
"Based on this proposal, the ministry submitted an appeal letter on Aug 13. However, in a letter dated Sept 23, the PSD informed the ministry that the appeal could not be considered," it said.
The ministry said it valued the contributions of senior subject teachers in overseeing subjects and improving schools' academic performance.
"The ministry is also committed to safeguarding teachers' welfare and will continue to work with all stakeholders, including unions and relevant agencies, to ensure the well-being of the teaching community," it said.

Title: Trump says US will stop $4 billion military aid to Israel at end of 2026
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and that Washington would no longer be providing military aid to Israel after the end of this year.
Speaking to Fox News' Fox and Friends, Trump said Israel no longer needs it and that some Democrats and left-wing politicians were using this US funding to Israel as a talking point to criticize Republicans.
"Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping," Trump told Fox News' Fox and Friends.
"We've already agreed that by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel. Now we'll help Israel if they need it."

Title: Police arrest woman seen in video causing ruckus, hitting children in mall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A woman who allegedly caused a disturbance and harassed other people in a shopping mall here recently has been arrested by police in Bandar Sri Damansara today.
Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the 25-year-old woman was arrested about 5.40pm.
"Police have arrested a local woman to assist in investigations into a case involving the harassment of visitors and customers at a shopping mall, which was reported on Nov 1.
"The woman admitted to being involved in the incident when she was questioned by investigators," he said in a statement.
It was previously reported that police were tracking down a woman suspected of harassing visitors at a shopping mall in the capital.
This was after police received three reports concerning incidents in which the woman allegedly shoved and assaulted visitors.
Police also received another report which claimed the
woman had shoved and hit her two children
in an incident that occurred on the same day.

Title: Anwar orders Sungai Buloh, Sungai Damansara flood mitigation projects to be expedited
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered work on the Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara flood mitigation projects to be expedited following repeated flooding in the area.
He said the two projects, costing nearly RM700 million and already approved by the federal government, must proceed without delay to minimise the risk of further flooding.
"Our priority is to speed things up. I have instructed that work such as river dredging, for which contracts have already been awarded, be expedited.
"What concerns me is that this area has been flooded two or three times. We need to widen the rivers, build additional retention ponds and carry out comprehensive flood mitigation measures," he told reporters after visiting the flood relief centre at the Siantan hall in Kampung Melayu Subang today.
Anwar said he would obtain a progress report on the federal government's flood mitigation projects this Friday, while Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari is expected to present an update on state-level projects at the state executive council meeting on the same day.
The Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara flood mitigation projects, comprising two phases, were previously approved with a total allocation of nearly RM700 million and are currently between 30 and 60 per cent complete.
On assistance for affected residents, Anwar gave his assurances that the government would provide additional aid to help ease the burden on flood victims.
He said the amount of assistance would be determined in consultation with the state government, taking into account each family's circumstances, particularly the extent of damage to their homes caused by the floods.
Yesterday, floods hit several areas in Subang and Sungai Buloh, including Jalan Jati, Kampung Melayu Subang and Kampung Kubu Gajah, with floodwaters reaching depths of between 0.3 and 0.6m.

Title: Radzi wants action taken against UNHCR for refugee registration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An opposition member of parliament wants action taken against the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.
Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) said this was because the organisation was still registering people despite a cabinet decision for it to stop.
"If the government's decision is to stop, then stop. UNHCR must stop, and the government must ensure that it stops registering any new refugees. This is the right of our country as a sovereign nation," he said.
Radzi was debating the 2027 Supply Bill at the committee stage in the Dewan Rakyat.
He warned against letting the public feel that UNHCR "does as it pleases".
"We must not wait for the people to take to the streets," he said.
He cited a July 23 Dewan Negara reply by Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni that the cabinet had told UNHCR to stop registering refugees while the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme was restructured.
The National Security Council (NSC) later said the rise in refugees was due to outstanding applications, he said.
"Who holds power in this country now? The cabinet decided that UNHCR must stop registering any new refugees," he said.
He claimed a UNHCR registration card dated Oct 29 this year had gone viral on social media, and that he visited the UNHCR website and found he could still enter details for Malaysia.
Lukanisman affirmed in winding-up for his ministry that the policy was to direct UNHCR to stop all registrations.
"However, we acknowledge that monitoring of UNHCR's process may not yet have been tightened, because we are finalising the use of the DPP card for registration under a module introduced by the Malaysian government," he said.
Lukanisman said there was still a backlog that had not been processed.
"The DPP has shown that we can register the refugees ourselves. However, we still face manpower constraints in carrying out registration on a large scale," he said.
Lukanisman said Malaysia could not reject UNHCR outright immediately.
"We have stated our position that they should stop registration.
"At the same time, we need to refine what the balance is of the refugees still on UNHCR's list, so that there are no errors or abuse of registration by UNHCR that could create bigger issues between Malaysia and the body," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Theta Edge's unit secures RM33.01mil contract to supply personal computers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Theta Edge Bhd's unit, Theta Technologies Sdn Bhd, has secured a RM33.01 million exclusive contract from Aceteam Networks Sdn Bhd to procure and supply up to 5,742 laptops and desktop computers under a device as a service (DaaS) lifecycle management project.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, it said the appointment will commence on the first delivery date. It will remain in force for five years from the date of the successful completion of the User Acceptance Test.
Aceteam Networks is a Malaysian information technology solutions provider, the filing said.
"The appointment represents an opportunity for Theta Edge and its subsidiaries to leverage existing capabilities and expertise of Theta Technologies in the technology and information technology solutions business.
"Through the appointment, Theta Technologies is expected to expand its business activities in the procurement and supply of computer hardware, thereby providing an opportunity to generate additional revenue and strengthen its business relationship with Aceteam," it said.
-- BERNAMA

Title: Taiwanese man to be charged over drug-fuelled crash involving policeman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 52-year-old Taiwanese man who crashed into a police escort rider in Brickfields on Friday, while driving under the influence of drugs, will be charged tomorrow.
City Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the man will face a charge under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for driving under the influence of drugs and causing injury.
He said the foreigner will also face charges under sections 39A(1) and 15(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 in a separate drug investigation handled by the Dang Wangi Narcotics Crime Investigation Department.
The crash occurred in Jalan Tun Sambanthan about 8.50pm as a 42-year-old policeman attached to the KL TEID motorcycle unit was returning from escort duty.
Zamzuri said the foreigner, who was travelling from Ampang towards Brickfields, crashed into the policeman, who sustained injuries to his legs and hands.
He said the man attempted to flee but was detained by another motorcycle unit policeman.
"The injured policeman was taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital for treatment.
"A breathalyser test on the driver returned a negative result for alcohol.
"However, a search of his vehicle uncovered a packet containing pills suspected to be ecstasy," he said.
He added that a preliminary urine test on the man returned positive for methamphetamine, ketamine and amphetamine.
Zamzuri said the suspect was remanded for four days from Nov 1 to assist investigations.
"Today, the investigation papers were referred to the Kuala Lumpur prosecution director at the Attorney-General's Chambers and the suspect was ordered to be charged."
He is scheduled to be charged at the magistrate's court in Jalan Duta.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Xi mourns Liu Yandong, rare woman official among China's Communist elite
Article:
BEIJING: President Xi Jinping attended a "solemn" ceremony in Beijing on Tuesday to mourn Liu Yandong, one of only a handful of women to have sat on the Chinese Communist Party's elite Politburo, state media reported.
Liu, a former vice premier, died on October 28 "due to illness" in Beijing, according to state news agency Xinhua. She was 80.
In 2007, Liu ascended to the 25-member Politburo at China's 17th Party Congress.
She was one of six women that have been a full member of the top policymaking body, which today is all men.
She held that seat until 2017 when she retired from the Politburo, though she remained a vice premier until 2018.
Liu graduated from Beijing's prestigious Tsinghua University where she was associated with former Chinese leader Hu Jintao.
During her political career she oversaw health, education, science, culture and sport, as well as women's and children's issues.
Liu met then-US secretary of state Hillary Clinton multiple times, with the two embracing as they greeted one another in Washington in 2011.
"We are the two mothers," Clinton joked, referencing a proposal to expand exchanges between people of the two countries.
On Tuesday, the Xinhua report praised Liu as a "loyal Communist fighter." She was cremated the same day at the Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery in Beijing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Emaar considers buyout of construction arm valued at nearly US$14bil
Article:
DUBAI real estate developer Emaar Properties is considering a plan to acquire its construction arm Emaar Development in a potential deal worth as much as US$3 billion, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday.
Emaar Properties, which owns just over 79 per cent of Emaar Development, could announce plans for a transaction within days, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Reuters could not immediately verify the Bloomberg report. Emaar did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Emaar Development has a market capitalisation of US$13.68 billion, according to LSEG data.
Emaar Properties is due to hold a board meeting this week to assess the proposal and has sought legal and financial advice, the Bloomberg report said, adding that deliberations are ongoing and no final decisions have been made.
Emaar, the developer of the Burj Khalifa - the world's tallest building - has played a central role in the emirate becoming the Gulf's business and tourism hub, including in the years following the Covid-19 pandemic when the property market boomed.
In June, Emaar announced plans for a nearly US$55 billion urban district in Dubai that would house 150,000 residents, wagering the emirate's property market can absorb the shock of regional conflict.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Solarvest strengthens leadership for next growth phase
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Solarvest Holdings Bhd has appointed Joseph Wong Aik Peoy as chief executive officer of engineering and operations.
The company also appointed James Lee Chung Min as chief energy transition officer as it expands into energy storage, grid modernisation and intelligent energy solutions.
Solarvest said in a statement today that the appointments are aimed at strengthening its leadership team to support a growing project pipeline and broader portfolio amid rising demand for flexible power and renewable energy integration.
Wong brings nearly 20 years of experience across renewable energy, oil and gas and major infrastructure projects.
He has held leadership positions at a global integrated energy group and an international engineering, procurement and construction company.
He will oversee engineering and operations, focusing on project execution, operational efficiency and adopting artificial intelligence (AI)-powered systems to improve project monitoring, reporting and risk management.
Lee, meanwhile, has 16 years of experience in Malaysia's renewable energy industry, covering technology innovation, industry advocacy and regulatory engagement.
He has contributed to national technical standards and consultations on key renewable energy programmes.
This includiles the Net Energy Metering scheme, Solar Accelerated Transition Action Programme and Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme.
He will lead Solarvest's energy transition strategy, focusing on technology adoption, industry collaboration and regional market development.
Group chief executive officer Dato' Davis Chong Chun Shiong said the appointments will combine stronger project execution with technological innovation as Solarvest moves beyond renewable energy generation.
He said energy storage, intelligent energy management and grid modernisation would become increasingly important as renewable energy penetration rises.

Title: ES Sunlogy's unit secures contracts worth RM25.07mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ES Sunlogy Bhd's wholly-owned subsidiary, Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd (Savelite), has secured two letters of award (LOAs) from Kerjaya Prospek (M) Sdn Bhd for sub-works contracts worth a combined RM25.07 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the engineering services company said Savelite secured a sub-works contract for the supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of electrical and extra low voltage (ELV) works for a 52-storey service apartment construction in Pulau Andaman, Penang.
"The RM19.87 million contract commenced on July 1, 2026. It is scheduled for completion by Dec 31, 2029, subject to time extension in accordance with LOA provisions," the filing said.
ES Sunlogy said the other contract involves infrastructure works for five canal bridges in Pulau Andaman, Penang, valued at RM5.20 million.
"The contract commenced on Nov 24, 2025. It is scheduled for completion on Aug 23, 2028, or by any extension of time provisions in the LOA," said ES Sunlogy.
According to the company, Savelite's acceptance of the contracts is expected to contribute positively to its net assets per share, earnings per share and gearing throughout the contract duration.
The LOAs will not affect the company's share capital and substantial shareholdings.
"Additionally, the sub-contract works are considered as a related-party transaction because Kerjaya Prospek (M), being the transacting party, is a company within the group of companies under Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd.
"ES Sunlogy had obtained its shareholders' mandate for related party transactions entered into or to be entered into by the group with the Kerjaya Group, its subsidiaries and joint ventures at its extraordinary general meeting held on Oct 21, 2026," it added.

Title: MM Computer bags RM51.58mil GPU servers order
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MM Computer Systems Bhd has secured a RM51.58 million order to supply enterprise-grade, graphics processing unit (GPU)-accelerated servers to a Malaysian telecommunications infrastructure and data centre services provider.
The order was received and accepted by its wholly-owned subsidiary Micro Technology Solution Sdn Bhd, the company said in a statement today.
The servers are designed to handle computationally intensive workloads.
This includes generative artificial intelligence (AI), large language model training and inference, deep learning, advanced data analytics and high-performance computing.
MM Computer said the purchase order is expected to contribute to its earnings per share and net assets per share.
The contract strengthens the company's business pipeline as demand for advanced computing infrastructure grows alongside the adoption of AI and other high-performance computing technologies, it added.

Title: Pekat gets SC nod for Main Market move
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pekat Group Bhd has secured the Securities Commission (SC) approval to transfer its listing from Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market to the Main Market.
The regulator granted its approval on Tuesday, Pekat said in a Bursa Malaysia filing.
The SC also confirmed that the group had complied with the Bumiputera equity requirement for public-listed companies.
The proposed transfer comes more than five years after Pekat made its ACE Market debut in June 2021.
Pekat first announced its intention to move to the Main Market in June this year, saying the transfer would enhance its corporate profile and broaden its appeal to investors, particularly institutional funds.
The company has met the financial criteria for the transfer, including a minimum combined net profit of RM30 million over three financial years, with at least RM15 million in the latest financial year.
Pekat recorded a cumulative net profit of RM80.78 million for financial years 2023 to 2025, including RM45.05 million in FY25.
Its revenue more than doubled to RM609.53 million in FY25 from RM286.98 million a year earlier, supported by stronger contributions from its solar and power distribution equipment businesses.
For the first six months of FY26, its net profit rose to RM26.63 million from RM23.08 million in the corresponding period last year, while revenue increased to RM343.32 million from RM277.30 million.
Pekat is involved in solar power systems, lightning protection and electrical equipment.
It had a market capitalisation of RM2.06 billion based on its five-day volume-weighted average share price as at Oct 30.
Public Investment Bank Bhd is the principal adviser for the proposed transfer.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Heavy rain sparks flood fears among Kampung Melayu Subang residents
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Residents of Kampung Melayu Subang, Shah Alam, fear flash floods could hit the area again following heavy rain today.
On Threads, several users shared pictures and videos showing floodwaters beginning to inundate roads, with some reporting rising water levels over the past few hours.
One of them was user @lxmonadxjuicxx who posted a video of her wading through a flooded road.
Another user, @gadissanwics, shared a picture of personal belongings damaged by flooding yesterday, saying rising waters were again approaching the fence of her house today.
"I haven't even finished cleaning up from yesterday," the user wrote.
Meanwhile, parts of Bandar Tun Hussein Onn in Cheras and Petaling Jaya were reported to have been hit by heavy rain and strong winds.
Food truck operator @therumi.kl also shared pictures of a business tent in Bandar Tun Hussein Onn destroyed by strong winds.
"In the blink of an eye, the scorching sunshine turned into a storm. Please pray for The Rumi team.
"The storm in BTHO this evening was something else. Tables were flying and tents were broken," the user wrote.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Media Prima presents aid to Kampung Seberang Alor fire victims [WATCH]
Article:
KANGAR: Media Prima Bhd (MPB), through the NSTP-Media Prima Disaster Relief Fund, today presented over RM34,000 in public donations to victims of a fire in Kampung Seberang Alor, Kuala Perlis.
The contribution was distributed to 10 heads of households whose homes were damaged in the fire, to help them rebuild their houses.
MPB Group chairman Datuk Seri Dr Syed Hussian Aljunid presented the aid to Perlis Social Welfare Department (JKM) director Ku Chik Ku Mat Esa, in the presence of the Raja Muda of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail.
On June 13, eight houses were completely destroyed while two others were damaged in a fire at Kampung Seberang Alor, within the Kuala Perlis Royal Village, here.
MPB Group general manager of corporate communications and the Group Chairman's Office, Azlan Abdul Aziz, said the handover fulfilled the trust placed in the fund by donors, with assistance distributed according to the extent of damage suffered by each affected family.
"On behalf of MPB, we wish to express our deepest gratitude to Tuanku Syed Faizuddin for graciously consenting to attend and witness today's handover ceremony. We also wish to record our appreciation to JKM Perlis and the Perlis Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council (MAIPs) for their continued support in making relief missions such as this a success.
"This contribution reflects the deep concern shown by Malaysians in helping disaster victims across the country. This is also not the first time we have extended assistance to fire victims, as we recently handed over similar contributions in Kota Bharu, Kelantan," he said when met after the ceremony.
At the same ceremony, Koperasi Sahabat Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM) Bhd also contributed RM10,000 to assist the fire victims.
Those who wish to contribute can channel their donations to the NSTP-Media Prima Disaster Relief Fund through Bank Muamalat account number 14010008843712.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hafidz Othman appointed new Prisons commissioner-general
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prisons Department deputy commissioner-general (Rehabilitation) Hafidz Othman has been appointed the department's new commissioner-general.
His appointment takes effect on Nov 5.
In a statement, the department said Hafidz received his appointment letter from Public Service director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz.
"Hafidz holds a Bachelor of Laws from Universiti Teknologi Mara and began his career as a deputy superintendent at Miri Prison in Sarawak.
"Throughout his 32 years of service, he has held various positions, including as director of the Seremban Prison and the Negeri Sembilan Prisons Department."
Hafidz has also served as director of the International Affairs and Transfer of Prisoners Division and director of the Prisons Department's Corrective Division.
He takes over from Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Razak, who retired in August.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Deepavali: 40,000 festive baskets worth RM5mil distributed in Johor
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Some 40,000 Deepavali baskets worth more than RM5 million were distributed to Indian households across Johor.
Separately, the state government has allocated RM1.87 million for the Jualan Kasih Johor programme, offering 54,000 subsidised essential-goods packages at RM15 each across 63 locations statewide.
Each package comprised a whole chicken, a tray of eggs and two litres of cooking oil.
Johor MIC chief K. Raven Kumar said the state government's initiatives were aimed at ensuring families could celebrate Deepavali while easing the financial burden of purchasing essential goods for the festivities.
The Kemelah assemblyman said the baskets, containing essential items such as cooking oil, rice, sugar and festive cookies, were distributed through the service centres of the state's 56 constituencies over the weekend.
[[nid:1570132]]
He said the initiative reflected the state government's commitment to ensuring that no community was left out of its development and welfare programmes.
He added that Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi had also been addressing long-standing issues affecting the Indian community, including those involving temples, burial grounds and housing.
"The people are happy with the state government and look forward to more incentives and initiatives, particularly those involving the younger generation," he said.
[[nid:1570131]]
Raven said the state was also looking at ways to ensure Indian youths benefited from opportunities arising from the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
"Onn Hafiz places strong emphasis on youth development. We want to ensure Indian youths also have access to the opportunities and benefits created by the JS-SEZ," he said.
Raven will host a Deepavali open house at his home in Bandar Putra, Segamat, on the first day of the festival, from 7pm.
He wished Hindus a happy Deepavali and urged families to celebrate with loved ones while remembering the elderly and underprivileged.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Touted as Waze alternative, TuJu now redirects users to Google Maps
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: TuJu users are now being redirected to Google Maps when they tap the navigation button.
This comes following the app's latest update amid efforts to resolve navigation disruptions.
The Android update, version 2.0.4, released on Oct 30, replaces TuJu's in-app navigation with Google Maps.
A New Straits Times test found that tapping "Navigation" prompted a pop-up informing users that Google Maps would open to continue their journey.
The existing iOS version also redirects users to Google Maps, although it remains listed as version 1.5.5, last updated in November 2025.
On Oct 21, the government
banned civil servants
from using Waze, citing the app's Israeli origins, prompting the promotion of TuJu as an alternative navigation app.
The app experienced disruptions a day after the government announced plans to switch to TuJu as an alternative to Waze.
TuJu later
apologised for navigation disruptions,
saying restoration work was expected to be completed by Nov 6.
Its developer, Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd, said its technical team was carrying out recovery and improvement work to ensure its features operated smoothly and reliably.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Status won't protect domestic violence perpetrators, says Penang exco member
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A person's social status, background or public standing will not protect him or her from action against domestic violence.
Social Development, Welfare and Non-Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Lim Siew Khim said no one was above the law.
"Domestic violence does not discriminate based on position, title, or social status.
"Whether an individual is an ordinary member of the public, a public figure, or an elected representative, everyone is equally accountable under the law," she said in a statement in response to allegations of domestic violence involving a Penang assemblyman.
Lim, however, said police must first be allowed to conduct a thorough investigation into the matter without interference.
"At this stage, it would be inappropriate to draw conclusions or make judgments against any party before the facts have been established.
"If any wrongdoing is proven, the necessary action must be taken in accordance with the law," she said, cautioning against the spread of unverified information.
Yesterday, police said they recorded statements from four people, including a Penang assemblyman and his wife, over an
alleged domestic assault
involving the couple.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim had confirmed that a police report was lodged and investigations were ongoing under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which concerns voluntarily causing hurt
Lim said the case serves as a stark reminder that domestic abuse remains a pressing societal concern requiring ongoing vigilance and comprehensive victim-support mechanisms.
She said the Penang government continues to tackle domestic abuse through initiatives like the Safe Family Policy, rolled out in 2020 in partnership with the Women's Centre for Change (WCC) and Penang Women's Development Corporation (PWDC).
Under the initiative, frontline personnel across state constituency service centres, government departments, and non-governmental organisations are trained as First Support Points (FSPs) to assist victims.
To date, 536 community members and organisational representatives have been trained under the network.
The state has also introduced the "Penang Stop Violence" mobile app to help survivors locate the nearest FSP and access emergency guidance.
"Victims of domestic violence should never feel that they have nowhere to turn. We want to ensure that anyone facing violence knows that support, protection, and assistance are available, regardless of their circumstances," Lim said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jais tracking owners of Puchong warehouse in 6.5-tonne halal chicken probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Selangor Islamic Religious Affairs Department (Jais) is tracking down the owners of a Puchong warehouse where more than 6.5 tonnes of
raw chicken
were seized over halal violations.
Its director, Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad, said Jais was working with the District and Land Office to obtain details on the registered company and the actual owners of the premises.
Jais' investigations found that the premises had no proper signage, halal certification application records or a Halal Certification Certificate.
Shahzihan said the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) had never issued slaughterer certification for activities at the site.
"Our records also indicate that operations at the premises were carried out by more than one company or entity," he said.
In the Oct 30 raid, 12 Bangladeshi and Pakistani men, believed to be workers at the facility, were arrested.
It was later found that the chickens had been electrocuted before being slaughtered.
Shahzihan said Jais was investigating the case under Section 4(1) of the Trade (Halal Definition) Act and Section 121F of the Islamic Religious Administration (Selangor) Enactment.
The sections cover passing off items as halal without meeting the requirements and carrying out halal slaughtering without a valid certificate. The offences carry jail terms and fines.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib fundraising drive still short of target, says Umno sec-gen [WATCH]
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Public donations to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak continue to come in, although the fundraising drive has yet to reach its target to cover his fine.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said daily collections averaged between RM5,000 and RM10,000.
He said contributions had come from people across all walks of life, including those who donated as little as RM1, RM5 and RM10.
"The momentum is good. I have observed that daily contributions from the public average between RM5,000 and RM10,000, including donations as small as RM10, RM5 and even RM1.
"This is what we call crowdfunding, where members of the public contribute to help Najib," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the Program Santai Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki bersama pengundi at the Durian Tunggal state constituency operations room in Taman Angkasa Nuri here today.
Also present were BN candidate for the Durian Tunggal seat Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa and former assemblyman Datuk Zahari Khalil.
Asyraf Wajdi said the fundraising effort was still ongoing, but the total amount collected had yet to be disclosed as the party wanted to wait for an appropriate time to announce it.
"God willing, I am confident, but I want to keep an element of surprise. We will make the announcement when the time comes," he said.
On political opponents continuing to raise Najib's name during the Melaka election campaign, Asyraf Wajdi said he believed the public still remembered the former prime minister's administration, particularly its impact on people's lives and the country's economy.
It was  previously reported that Najib had yet to pay the RM50 million fine, based on the latest information from the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC).
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said no specific deadline had been set for payment of the fine and confirmed that Najib would have to remain in prison until it was paid.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rayer: Why hasn't Zakir Naik been extradited, who pays for apartment, bodyguards?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) has questioned why the government will not extradite preacher Dr Zakir Naik to India.
"I would like to ask why. He is someone who has stirred up various controversies," he said in the Dewan Rakyat here while debating the 2027 Supply Bill at the committee stage.
He said he understood that Zakir lived in a luxury apartment in Putrajaya and asked who bore the cost.
"I also understand that whenever he goes out for any event, personal bodyguards are provided.
"Who bears the cost of his bodyguards? Does the government bear the cost?"
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had said earlier that the government had decided
not to extradite Zakir
and had made no commitment to hand him over to India.
Rayer recalled that Zakir gave a speech in Kota Baru on Aug 8, 2019, questioning the loyalty of Malaysian citizens of Indian and Chinese descent.
"This angered Malaysian citizens of Indian and Chinese descent, and police reports were lodged," he said.
Rayer's debate was interrupted by Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman (PN-Sik), who said Zakir was outside the Dewan Rakyat and could not respond.
"I am not giving way... this is my time. I do not want to be interrupted," Rayer replied.
Deputy Speaker Alice Lau told Tarmizi to sit down and not interrupt.
Rayer then repeated his question to the government.
"So, I ask the government for an explanation, and I want to know why he is not being sent back to India," he said.
Earlier, Saifuddin said the decision was based on Malaysia's rights under Article 6 of the extradition treaty signed with the Indian government in 2010, as well as provisions under the Extradition Act 1992.
He said the government had not received any new extradition request from India concerning Zakir.
The Indian government had submitted an official extradition request on Jan 19, 2018, followed by a diplomatic note seeking a review of the decision on May 29, 2020.
The calls for clarification over Zakir's extradition followed media reports that the matter, sought by India over allegations of money laundering and hate speech, was discussed in talks between Anwar and Indian representatives.
Indian news outlet New Delhi Television (NDTV) reported that Anwar had confirmed the matter was discussed behind closed doors, in New Delhi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SP Setia unit, Help seal deal for Kinrara International School
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SP Setia Bhd's unit Perumahan Kinrara Bhd and Help Kinrara Sdn Bhd have signed a build-and-lease agreement for a new international school in Bandar Kinrara.
SP Setia will develop the purpose-built campus, and Help will lease and operate it as the fourth school in the group, targeted to open in August 2029.
The international school will be developed on a 0.81-hectare site within the 6.45-hectare commercial land parcel in Bandar Kinrara.
It is planned as a six-storey campus with an indicative gross floor area of 176,085 square feet and capacity for more than 1,000 students.
The international school intends to serve families in Bandar Kinrara and surrounding communities while contributing to a more integrated, accessible and liveable urban precinct.
It is expected to offer primary and secondary programmes based on the British Curriculum, incorporating the International Primary Curriculum and leading to Cambridge IGCSE qualifications, for students aged five to 16.
The campus is planned to include 55 classrooms, six science laboratories with preparation rooms, an engineering and design workshop, a food technology kitchen, two music rooms, two art rooms, dedicated edtech facilities, a library of about 4,200 square feet and a multipurpose hall that spans 6,000 square feet.
Under the agreements, Perumahan Kinrara will undertake the development and construction of the school complex.
Help will secure the required education approvals and complete the campus fit-out before the school opens.
"Setia's collaboration with Help reflects this approach to innovation, bringing complementary expertise into our townships to create places that offer more than a home.
"By integrating education into the wider vision for Bandar Kinrara, we aim to enhance everyday living for existing homeowners and give prospective buyers greater confidence in the community they choose to be part of," SP Setia president and chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Zaini Yusoff said in a statement.
"Beyond academic achievement, at the heart of every Help school is a commitment to nurturing the whole child and equipping them to be career and future ready for a fast-changing world.
"This commitment is reflected in our accreditation by the Council of International Schools, a testament to the care our leaders, teachers and staff bring to our schools every day," said Help Group co-CEO Dr Gerard Louis.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Private universities steal the spotlight as Malaysia sets a historic record in QS Asia 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — More than 50 Malaysian universities penetrated the QS World University Rankings Asia 2027 for the first time, with 11 emerging among the top 100 in Asia.
Overall, Malaysia is the eighth most represented higher education system in Asia, with 55 featured universities on the list. The country also stands on par with Japan and Korea with eight entries in the top 50.
Of the 16 Malaysian universities that achieved record-high positions for 2027, 12 were private universities.
They include Sunway University, INTI International University, Asia Pacific University of Technology and Innovation (APU), SEGi University, IMU University, MILA University, Tunku Abdul Rahman University of Management and Technology, Perdana University, Quest International University (QIU), Nilai University, UNITAR International University and Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah (UniSHAMS).
The highest-ranked private university was Taylor’s University at the 32nd spot, albeit dropping five spots from the previous edition.
Sunway University also ranked among the top 50 for the first time while INTI International University made it into the top 100 for the first time.
Universiti Malaya (UM) remained the country’s best-performing university, emerging among the top 20 universities in Asia for the ninth consecutive year despite slipping two spots to the 17th rank this edition.
Meanwhile, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) entered the top 20 for the first time, rising four spots from the previous edition while Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI) emerged top in Asia for the Faculty with PhD indicator.
260,000 international students by 2030
QS senior vice-president Ben Sowter said Malaysia has more than doubled the number of universities in the top 100 in the QS World University Rankings: Asia in the last decade. The number of universities in the top 50 has also increased from only two in 2017 to eight in 2027.
“Its renown as an education hub in Southeast Asia is only growing, and research from QS suggests that, by the end of the decade, international student numbers are projected to reach about 260,000,” Sowter said.
According to the 2027 edition, Malaysia has the most well-represented higher education system in two key indicators. It has 24 universities in the top 100 entries for the International Faculty indicator and 31 in the top 100 entries in the International Students indicator.
However, it only has one entry in the top 100 for Citations per Paper and Papers per Faculty indicators.
How did other countries perform?
The QS Asia University Rankings 2027 evaluated 1722 universities across 26 locations.
The University of Hong Kong retained the top spot in the ranking while Peking University and Tsinghua University from China finished second and third respectively.
Hong Kong also recorded the highest number of universities in the top 10 while Japan logged one of Asia’s highest drop rates.
Meanwhile, Singapore’s two universities also dropped out of the top five, with the National University of Singapore (NUS) now ranking sixth in Asia while the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) Singapore settled at the eighth position.
Maldives also debuted this edition, featuring The Maldives National University and Villa College.

Title: Hafidz Othman appointed new Prisons Department chief, takes office on Nov 5
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — Deputy Commissioner General of Prisons (Community) Hafidz Othman has been appointed the new Commissioner General of Prisons, effective Nov 5, the Prisons Department said.
In a statement today, the department said Hafidz received his appointment letter from Public Service director-general Tan Sri Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz.
He will succeed Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Razak, who has held the post since Feb 14, 2025.
Hafidz, who holds a Bachelor of Laws degree from Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), began his career as a prison officer with the rank of Deputy Superintendent at Miri Prison in Sarawak.
During his 32 years of service, he has held several key positions, including heading Seremban Prison, Negeri Sembilan Prisons, the International Affairs and Prisoner Transfer Division, and the Correctional Division, according to the statement.
He also served as Deputy Commissioner General of Prisons (Management) in 2025.
The department expressed hope that Hafidz would draw on his experience, expertise and leadership to further strengthen its correctional services, in line with the aspirations of Malaysia Madani and the Public Service Reform Agenda. — Bernama

Title: Govt pays RM20.27b in income tax refunds to 3.65m taxpayer cases as at Oct 31
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — A total of RM20.271 billion in income tax refunds involving 3.65 million taxpayer cases had been paid as at Oct 31, 2026.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said of the total, RM6.84 billion had been refunded to 3.4 million individual taxpayers, while RM13.036 billion had been refunded to 206,234 corporate taxpayers, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
“In carrying out the refunds, the government prioritises excess tax refunds to individuals as well as MSMEs,” he said during the winding-up session of the Supply Bill at the committee stage for the Ministry of Finance (MoF) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Amir Hamzah also said that, in line with this approach, the number of taxpayers with excess tax credits had been reduced by almost half to about 550,000 as at Oct 31, 2026, compared with more than one million as at Dec 31, 2025.
“The government is also committed to ensuring that outstanding tax refunds are fully settled promptly, as part of efforts to improve tax administration efficiency and safeguard taxpayers’ rights, in line with the Madani government’s fiscal reform agenda,” he said in response to questions raised by Members of Parliament (MPs) for Bachok, Klang and Pendang.
Amir Hamzah reiterated the government’s commitment to addressing the backlog of excess income tax refunds to ensure that all outstanding payments are made promptly.
A total of 27 MPs took part in the committee-stage debate on the MoF.
He said the views and feedback raised would help the government review how each allocation was managed and implemented for the benefit of the people.
Overall, the 2027 operating supply expenditure allocation for the ministry increased to RM68.16 billion, compared with the revised allocation of RM61.5 billion for this year.
He said the increase reflected the Madani government’s commitment to easing the cost of living and ensuring the well-being of the people. — Bernama

Title: Johor identifies 337 flood hotspots as state braces for northeast monsoon
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Nov 3 — The Johor government will focus on 337 flood hotspots statewide as the northeast monsoon is expected to affect the state from this month until January next year.
State Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said priority would be given to areas with high population density and a history of major flooding, including the districts of Kota Tinggi, Batu Pahat and Segamat.
“Based on updates from the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), 35 flood hotspots, including new additions, have been identified.
“The Public Works Department (JKR) has also identified 30 high-risk road locations that comprise 21 sites on federal roads and nine on state roads,” he told reporters after a working visit to the Sungai Rinting flood wall project here today.
Also present were Permas assemblyman Baharudin Mohamed Taib and senior government agency officials.
Mohamad Fazli said the measures outlined included hotspot mapping, drain maintenance, cleaning and dredging drainage systems, ensuring machinery was ready, public outreach and the use of the eBencana (electronic disaster) reporting system.
He said the relevant projects included Phase 1 of the Sungai Johor Flood Mitigation Plan, the Sungai Pemandi Flood Mitigation Plan and a flood alleviation project in Kampung Sungai Kapal Lama in Pengerang.
In Batu Pahat, Mohamad Fazli said the DID had identified 41 flood hotspots, while the JKR had detected 21 high-risk locations along federal and state roads, covering a total distance of 6.5 kilometres.
He added that preparations would include road pavement maintenance works worth RM11.79 million, non-pavement works worth RM3.20 million and an allocation of RM1.92 million under the Malaysian Road Records Information System (MARRIS) for drainage-related works.
“Alternative route plans via the FT024 federal road and the PLUS Highway have also been planned.
“Mobile pumps at the Parit Botak sluice gate, flood mitigation projects – such as the Bandar Batu Pahat and Sungai Batu Pahat flood mitigation schemes – as well as coastal embankment upgrading works, are also being given due attention,” he said.
In Segamat, Mohamad Fazli said the DID had identified 29 flood hotspots, while the JKR had identified 16 high-risk locations, comprising eight federal roads and eight state roads.
“Efforts are also focused on monitoring river levels and roadways, as well as coordinating with the Batu Pahat district, which is located downstream,” he said.
In Muar, he said 65 flood hotspots had been identified, the highest number among the districts listed by the DID.
In Tangkak, 26 hotspots had been identified, with priority measures including inspecting culverts and drainage systems, monitoring roadways and coordinating maintenance efforts among the relevant agencies.
Mohamad Fazli said there were also 44 flood hotspots in Johor Bahru, 29 in Kluang, 19 in Pontian, 27 in Kulai and 22 in Mersing.
In a related development, he said the state government was preparing an application for an emergency allocation of between RM20 million and RM30 million to carry out maintenance works and flood preparedness measures in high-risk areas throughout November and December.
“Priority will be given to tasks that can be executed immediately, specifically maintenance work, whereas large-scale projects, such as the construction of embankments and flood-retaining walls, will require a longer timeframe,” he added.

Title: After Customs flags import irregularities, maritime expert asks MACC to revisit RM220m crude cargo report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — A maritime industry executive today asked whether the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) would take further action on his report over alleged discrepancies in petroleum cargo records, following the Royal Malaysian Customs Department’s latest disclosure on import declaration irregularities.
Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan lodged the report on June 5 over alleged discrepancies between bills of lading and the physical movement of petroleum cargo at Tanjung Langsat Port, Johor, in transactions reportedly worth millions of ringgit.
The report involved two petroleum cargoes totalling 76,954.325 metric tonnes of Atlanta Crude, valued at more than RM220 million, which were discharged at Tanjung Langsat.
Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of experience in the maritime industry, questioned whether the latest information from Customs could give MACC grounds to revisit the concerns raised in his report.
Customs director-general Datuk Seri Amran Ahmad was quoted by
Harian Metro
as saying that certain importers had allegedly manipulated documents, under-declared the value, weight and quantity of imported goods, and used incorrect tariff codes to evade or reduce import duties and taxes.
Amran said this could potentially result in millions of ringgit in revenue losses to the government.
Jeyenderan said the key concern was traceability, particularly how the authorities and relevant parties could establish what happened to the cargo after it entered storage tanks containing existing inventory, including any subsequent movement, mixing or blending.
He said the relevant records should show the quantity discharged into each tank, the existing inventory, subsequent product movements, laboratory specifications and the quantities eventually removed or transferred, to ensure an unbroken documentary trail.
He stressed that Maritime Network had acted only as the vessel or shipping agent for the cargo movements, and was not the cargo owner, terminal operator, laboratory or Customs authority.
As such, he said, the roles and responsibilities of all parties involved must be clearly established.
Jeyenderan wants MACC to clarify whether the Customs disclosure warrants further investigation, particularly regarding the accuracy of cargo declarations and the applicable regulatory treatment.
He said the main concern was whether the cargo declarations, supporting documents and actual physical movement of the petroleum products were consistent with the relevant Customs requirements.
He also called on the authorities to clarify whether there were any regulatory or revenue implications arising from the handling of petroleum cargoes, particularly where shared storage tanks and blending arrangements were involved.

Title: New law replacing AUKU will not curtail students’ freedom of expression, says Zahid
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 3 — The new Bill to replace the now-repealed Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) will not affect students’ freedom of expression, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said the Cabinet agreed that the proposed legislation would be limited to matters concerning university administration, including academic affairs, governance and the appointment of senate members,
Ahmad Zahid also said that the new law would also cover the selection of university management personnel, including vice-chancellors and deputy vice-chancellors.
“The new legislation, which will carry a different name, will no longer include the seven provisions concerning students, including those on freedom, under AUKU, which restricted their freedom to engage in activities,” he said.
He was asked about the latest developments in the proposal for a new law to replace AUKU after attending the Apa Khabar Mahasiswa: Patriotisme Diperkasa programme at Universiti Teknologi Mara’s (UiTM) Alor Gajah Campus in Melaka today.
Also present at the event was Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir.
Ahmad Zahid, also the Rural and Regional Development Minister, said universities should not penalise students for expressing their opinions unless their remarks involved sensitive issues relating to race, religion and the royal institution (3R).
“Under AUKU, universities did take action against students. Now that the Act has been repealed, students remain subject to existing laws, including criminal legislation.
“...if students are simply expressing differing opinions, political beliefs or the views of young people, I believe universities should welcome this rather than take legal action against them, unless their actions breach the law,” he said.
In a separate development, Ahmad Zahid said enrolment for the Department of Quantum Technology at UiTM was expected to begin next semester under a training-for-trainers concept.
“Initially, the academic staff will be sent for master’s or PhD studies, or short courses, to equip those with backgrounds in information technology and digital technology to lead the department before it is upgraded to the Faculty of Quantum Technology,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid announced earlier in October that RM500,000 would be allocated as initial funding to establish UiTM’s Department of Quantum Technology. — Bernama

Title: Govt approves over RM250m for ECRL expansion plans and new Kota Bharu bus terminal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — The Madani government has approved more than RM250 million to strengthen the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) development in Kelantan, according to the Ministry of Finance (MOF).
This includes building a new bus terminal at the Kota Bharu ECRL Station and preliminary works for a proposed extension to Rantau Panjang, said the ministry in a statement today.
Of the total, RM30 million has been allocated for the new bus terminal, while more than RM200 million will fund preliminary works for the proposed ECRL extension from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang.
“The preliminary works include initial design, land surveys and investigations, an environmental impact assessment (EIA), preparation of the Railway Scheme and site preparation works to facilitate the project’s implementation in the next phase,” it said.
The investment aims to enhance transport infrastructure and create opportunities for competitive economic development in Kelantan. The development is expected to spur business activities, strengthen the logistics sector, attract investment and create job opportunities for the local population, said MOF.
The ministry emphasised that national development must be inclusive and balanced to ensure that the benefits of progress reach people throughout the country, including in Kelantan, rather than being concentrated solely in major cities. — Bernama

Title: Fashion Valet trial: Investment funds cannot be used to pay dividends, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Sessions Court hearing the case involving Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd (Fashion Valet) founders Datin Vivy Sofinas Yusof and her husband, Datuk Fadzarudin Shah Anuar, was told today that investment funds could not be used to pay dividends to any party, including the company’s shareholders.
Corporate lawyer Anne Wong Wai Yee, 49, who was involved in drafting the shareholders’ agreement between the couple and seven other companies, including Fashion Valet, on March 5, 2018, said the agreement did not contain any provision allowing investment funds to be used for such payments.
The other six companies were Proven Holding Sdn Bhd, MY E.G. Capital Sdn Bhd, Transasia E-Commerce Inc., Start Today Co. Ltd., Reussi Sdn Bhd and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd.
“The declaration of dividends requires the approval of a majority of the directors, including those appointed by Start Today Co. Ltd. and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd,” she testified during the trial of the couple, who are facing charges of criminal breach of trust involving RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah Nasional Berhad (Khazanah) and Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB).
The sixth prosecution witness said the agreement also specified the permitted uses of the investment funds, namely expenditure on technology development, stores and warehouses, as well as products and brands.
“The permitted allocation of the investment funds was as follows: 30 per cent for consumer acquisition, 30 per cent for technology development, 20 per cent for store and warehouse expansion, and 20 per cent for product and brand acquisition, based on the total investment value.
“Typically, such expenditures require approval from a majority of the board of directors,” Wong said.
She said Fashion Valet was required to submit summaries of the utilisation of the investment funds to the board of directors on a quarterly and annual basis until the entire amount had been utilised.
“However, I have no knowledge of the distribution of dividends or the transfer of investment funds received by Fashion Valet, as my scope of work was limited to drafting and coordinating the contractual agreements.
“The subsequent execution of these agreements by the parties involved falls outside the scope of my professional duties,” said Wong, a partner at Karen Kaur & Anne Wong Partnership.
She further testified that Fashion Valet was prohibited from extending loans or credit to its directors, shareholders, related companies or any other parties without the approval of a majority of the board of directors.
“Furthermore, Fashion Valet is restricted from entering into any agreement or understanding with parties related to the company, its directors or shareholders, involving RM50,000 or more annually, without the approval of a majority of the directors, including those appointed by Start Today Co. Ltd. and Pulau Tiga Ventures Sdn Bhd,” she added.
Referring to a Subscription Agreement dated June 4, 2018, Wong said the document constituted a binding agreement between the relevant parties, namely Fashion Valet, Proven Holdings and PNB, concerning PNB’s investment in the company.
“Essentially, this agreement sets out the terms and conditions of PNB’s investment in Fashion Valet, whereby, in exchange for the investment, Fashion Valet would issue Redeemable Convertible Preference Shares (RCPS) to PNB,” she testified.
Vivy, 38, and Fadzarudin, 37, are charged with criminal breach of trust, allegedly committed with common intention in their capacity as directors of Fashion Valet, involving RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah and PNB.
The charge alleges that they had authorised payments totalling RM8 million from Fashion Valet’s corporate bank account to a company known as 30 Maple without the approval of the company’s board of directors.
The alleged offence took place at the Public Bank Berhad branch in Bukit Damansara, at 36-40 Medan Setia 2, Plaza Damansara, Bukit Damansara, on Aug 21, 2018.
The charge, under Section 409 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Code, provides for imprisonment of between two and 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
The couple also pleaded not guilty to an alternative charge of dishonestly misappropriating, with common intention, property belonging to Fashion Valet, namely RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah and PNB, at the same location and on the same date.
The alternative charge, under Section 403 of the Penal Code, carries a penalty of imprisonment of between six months and five years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
The trial, before Judge Rosli Ahmad, continues on Nov 20. — Bernama

Title: Traders risk RM100,000 fine for hidden charges, Parliament told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Traders who impose hidden charges or disclose additional fees only at the final stage of a transaction may face legal action, including fines of up to RM100,000, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the practice misled consumers and undermined their right to know the actual price before making a purchase.
“This means consumers should have clear information on the amount they need to pay, rather than discovering certain charges at the final stage of a transaction,” he said in a written reply in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Muhammad Islahuddin Abas (PN-Mersing) on measures taken by the ministry to curb the practice of imposing additional or hidden charges disclosed only at the final stage of a transaction, resulting in the actual price exceeding the displayed or advertised price, particularly in the services, food and beverage, and online transaction sectors.
Armizan said Section 10B(1) of the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011 [Act 723] allows action against businesses that fail to include all taxes, duties, and other charges in the prices of goods or services they display, advertise, publish, or quote.
The same Act stipulates under Section 57 that corporate bodies found in breach of the provision may be fined up to RM100,000, while individuals face penalties of up to RM50,000 in fines, two years’ imprisonment, or both.
He said the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) also had enforcement powers under the Consumer Protection Act 1999 [Act 599], particularly Section 12(1)(a), which makes misleading representations about the price of goods or services an offence.
Section 12(3)(c) of the Act further stipulates that a price display is considered misleading if it gives the impression that the stated price covers everything, when additional charges are in fact imposed separately.
“Sections 9 and 10 of the Act also prohibit false or misleading claims about the nature and characteristics of goods or services. The provisions cover both transactions at physical business premises and online transactions.
“Those found in breach of the relevant provisions may be penalised under Section 145 of Act 599. The penalty for corporate bodies is a fine of up to RM100,000, while individuals may be fined up to RM50,000, jailed for up to three years, or both,” he said.
Armizan said KPDN had introduced guidelines on the All-Inclusive Pricing Policy to promote price transparency, particularly in the food and beverage, e-commerce and delivery sectors, requiring consumers to be informed of the total price, including the base price, service charges and delivery fees, before confirming an order.
He said the ministry also enforced the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering (Price Marking of Goods and Charges for Services) Order 2020, which requires service providers and business premises to display clearly and prominently a list of services offered and the charges imposed.
“The ministry will continue to step up monitoring and enforcement to ensure traders comply with price disclosure requirements, and urges consumers to check the final price before making payment.
“Consumers should also report to KPDN any instances of hidden fees or discrepancies between advertised prices and the actual amounts charged,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Mount Kinabalu training centre faces calls to halt work over indigenous, environmental concerns
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 3 — The ongoing construction of a high-altitude training centre on Mount Kinabalu has come under scrutiny, with indigenous groups and tourism stakeholders questioning its environmental impact, approvals and whether communities with customary ties to the mountain were adequately consulted.
