The controversy surfaced around October 30 after photographs showing structures and apparent drilling activities near Sayat-Sayat circulated on social media, prompting calls for authorities to clarify the nature and purpose of the work.
The photographs prompted criticism over a lack of transparency, including from Kundasang Tourism and Culture Association chairman Datuk Japiril Suhaimin, who called for an investigation into the project's location, scope and approvals, as well as its potential effects on water sources, soil stability and biodiversity.
Bundu Tuhan Village Heritage and Culture head Adrian Soros also questioned whether communities with customary ties to the mountain had been consulted, saying many villagers were unaware of the construction.
He raised concerns about drilling into the mountain, which he said went against customary beliefs, as well as the protection of local water sources and the management of human waste at high altitude.
Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin subsequently issued a statement saying the project was not new and had originally been proposed under the Kinabalu Park Development Plan in 2015.
He said the project had obtained approval from the Sabah Parks Board of Trustees and endorsement from the Mount Kinabalu Native Customary Advisory Council.
“The HATC was originally proposed under the Kinabalu Park Development Plan in 2015, but its implementation was deferred following the earthquake that struck Mount Kinabalu that year.
“The initiative was subsequently revived and officially launched in 2025 as part of Sabah’s efforts to diversify its tourism offerings and strengthen its position as an internationally recognised mountaineering destination,” he said.
The new development would provide basic accommodation and specialised facilities to support high-altitude training and mountaineering activities.
Jafry said the centre was intended to cater to mountaineers preparing for expeditions to higher-altitude destinations, including Mount Kilimanjaro, Aconcagua and Mount Everest, by providing facilities for altitude acclimatisation, technical training and familiarisation with specialised climbing equipment.
He said construction involved lightweight, prefabricated and modular building materials to minimise environmental disturbance, with the structures designed to withstand strong winds and challenging weather conditions at higher elevations.
The construction method also avoided the use of heavy machinery in view of the mountain’s sensitive natural environment.
Jafry said the project’s approval and implementation must respect Mount Kinabalu’s cultural and spiritual significance to indigenous communities, as reflected in the involvement of the Native Customary Advisory Council.
The minister nevertheless emphasised that the approval did not exempt the project from complying with stipulated conditions, technical specifications and environmental regulations.
“We take the concerns raised by the public seriously. The ministry will consider a comprehensive investigation to ascertain whether all approved specifications, environmental safeguards and regulatory conditions have been fully observed.
“Should any non-compliance be established, the ministry will not hesitate to pursue the necessary enforcement measures in accordance with the law,” he said.
However, despite his statement, the Dayak International Organisation (DIO) today called for all construction, drilling and installation work at the site to stop, alleging that the development violated indigenous customary law protected under the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP).
Its United Nations representative, Datuk Petinggi Andrew Ambrose Atama Katama, questioned the use of the Mount Kinabalu Native Customary Advisory Council to endorse the project, saying this did not replace the need for consent from communities, particularly the Kadazandusun and Momogun.
Andrew described Aki Nabalu as a sacred living entity and ancestral repository rather than a commercial asset for generating state revenue.
DIO also called for an independent environmental audit, including an assessment of wastewater impact on local water catchments, and said it would raise the matter at the United Nations Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues and the Unesco Global Geoparks Network.
Mount Kinabalu, also known as Aki Nabalu, is Sabah's highest peak at 4,095 metres and holds deep cultural and spiritual significance for indigenous communities, particularly the Kadazandusun.
Every year, locals hold sacred rituals to honour the mountain spirits, seek permission and protection, and ensure the safety and well-being of climbers.
Kinabalu Park was inscribed as a Unesco World Heritage Site in 2000 for its exceptional biodiversity, including thousands of plant species and a wide range of habitats.

Title: Zahid denies trying to sabotage govt, says he has documents on cancelled rural projects
Article:
JASIN, Nov 3 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied allegations that he intended to sabotage the Madani Government by revealing the cancellation or postponement of rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, maintained that his remarks concerning the suspension or cancellation of Letters of Acceptance (SSTs) for the projects were factual, adding that he was prepared to produce official documents to substantiate his claims.
“I had no such intention (to sabotage the government). Whether the projects have been postponed or cancelled, the fact remains that there were instructions to cancel all SSTs that have been or are due to be issued.
“I have documentary evidence of the instructions. I can show it,” he told reporters after officiating the  Mara Higher Education and TVET Tour 2026 programme in Melaka here today.
Yesterday, Jelutong MP RSN Rayer, while interjecting during a debate in the Dewan Rakyat, questioned Ahmad Zahid’s statement concerning the cancellation of rural development projects in Sabah and Sarawak.
Rayer described the remarks as an attempt to sabotage the Madani Government. — Bernama

Title: KL steps up drainage checks ahead of rainy season to prevent flash floods, says Hannah Yeoh
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 3 — Spot checks on drainage systems and cleaning works in Kuala Lumpur are being stepped up to keep drains clear and reduce the risk of flash floods, especially during the rainy season.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said these checks must be carried out thoroughly, including during the dry season, to ensure cleaning works are done properly and drainage systems function well.
She said clean-looking roads do not necessarily mean the drainage system is in good condition, as drains may be blocked without anyone noticing.
“That is why, before the rainy season, during the dry season, we have already reminded them... we must carry out spot checks,” she told reporters after launching the Community-Based Eco Recycling Hub (COB3R) at Presint 9 here today.
Hannah said each parliamentary branch office has also activated teams to conduct patrols and channel the latest reports on flash flood-prone areas to the Kuala Lumpur mayor.
She said active monitoring is crucial to ensure flash flood hotspots, which were successfully reduced from 30 to 14 over the past three years, do not rise again.
“The goal for Kuala Lumpur is to bring it down further to 10,” she added.
Hannah also said the frequency of cleaning and desilting works on Sungai Toba has increased from twice to six times a year as part of efforts to reduce the risk of flash floods.
She said changing weather patterns and extraordinary heavy rainfall require the authorities to reassess existing standard operating procedures (SOPs) and improve disaster preparedness.
“With the current weather, the current rain, we cannot use ordinary SOPs. We must be prepared,” she said, adding that Kuala Lumpur’s development planning must also adopt the sponge city approach by preserving open and green spaces to help absorb rainwater.
She said development in hilly areas must be strictly controlled to ensure the area’s natural capacity to hold rainwater is not compromised.
“You cannot replace this green space with concrete. The water needs a place to go,” she said. — Bernama

Title: MCMC opens probe into Facebook post allegedly insulting Sultan of Selangor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has reportedly opened an investigation into a Facebook post suspected of containing highly offensive remarks against the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah.
According to
Bernama
, MCMC said in a statement today that the post was also suspected of touching on sensitivities involving race, religion and royalty (3R).
The commission said it had recorded a statement from the individual involved at the Sri Petaling police station to assist investigations.
A mobile phone and a SIM card were also seized as part of the investigation.
The case is being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, which carries a maximum fine of RM500,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
MCMC said it viewed seriously the spread of online content suspected of containing false information or insults against the royal institution, particularly material that could undermine social harmony.
The commission also reminded the public to use social media responsibly and refrain from creating or sharing content that violates Malaysian laws.

Title: Flood-hit Selangor districts back in firing line as MetMalaysia warns of torrential evening rain across 10 states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an evening thunderstorm warning across large swathes of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak until 8.00pm today, a day after torrential downpours triggered widespread flash floods across the Klang Valley.
The weather alert, released at 4.10pm, warns of severe thunderstorms, heavy rainfall, and gusty winds, placing commuters and low-lying neighbourhoods on high alert following Monday’s evening travel chaos.
In the peninsula, the advisory blankets the entirety of Perlis and Kedah, alongside all three mainland districts of Penang: Seberang Perai Utara, Seberang Perai Tengah, and Seberang Perai Selatan. Perak faces widespread disruption spanning 12 districts, including Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Muallim, Batang Padang, Larut Matang, Selama, Kerian, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, and Bagan Datuk.
Across Selangor, the advisory covers Hulu Selangor, Sabak Bernam, and Kuala Selangor, alongside Petaling and Klang, two major urban districts where drainage systems were inundated during Monday’s deluge.
In the south, the alert spans Batu Pahat, Muar, Tangkak, and Kluang in Johor.
East coast states are similarly braced for stormy weather. Kelantan faces downpours across Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Pasir Puteh, and Bachok. In Terengganu, the alert covers Besut, Hulu Terengganu, Setiu, and Dungun.
Across East Malaysia, the warning covers multiple divisions in Sarawak, including Lubok Antu in Sri Aman, Sarikei, Betong, Tanjung Manis in Mukah, Asajaya and Sebuyau in Samarahan, Marudi and Telang Usan in Miri, and Belaga in Kapit. In Sabah, the bulletin spans Ranau, Papar, Penampang, Tuaran, and Kota Kinabalu along the West Coast, alongside Tambunan, Membakut, Pensiangan, and Keningau in the Interior, Kalabakan in Tawau, and Tongod in Sandakan.
MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm advisories when satellite and radar indicators track rainfall intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that is either imminent or expected to persist beyond an hour. The department noted that these warnings serve as short-term alerts, valid for a maximum of six hours from issuance.
The alert follows Monday’s cloudburst that inundated arterial roads, submerged vehicles, and crippled the evening commute across the Klang Valley.
With ground saturation still high, authorities have urged motorists and residents in flood-prone zones to monitor real-time weather updates.

Title: AGC orders further police action in probe into claims Negeri Sembilan MB was forced to sign proclamation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 —The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) has returned investigation papers concerning allegations that Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was forced to sign an Instrument of Proclamation to the police for further action.
In a statement today, the AGC said it had reviewed the investigation papers submitted by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) on Oct 30 concerning the incident.
“An investigation was opened under Section 506 of the Penal Code after the Menteri Besar alleged that he had signed a proclamation concerning changes to the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan under undue influence.
“Following a comprehensive review, it was found that several further steps must be undertaken by the investigating officer before any decision can be made.
“Accordingly, the investigation papers will be returned to the PDRM today for further action,” the AGC said.
Yesterday, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar reportedly denied any delay by the AGC in reviewing investigation papers relating to a report involving Ismail. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says MotoGP 2026 success boosts Malaysia’s global motorsports standing and local economy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The success in staging the Petronas Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (MotoGP) 2026 has not only strengthened the country’s reputation as a host of world-class motorsports events, but also serves as a catalyst for local economic activity, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“The Petronas Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (MotoGP) 2026 once again proves the country’s ability to organise world-class sporting events that not only attract motorsports fans but also bring benefits to the people and the local economy,” he said in a Facebook post today.
He said the determination and support of all parties were among the key factors that contributed to the successful staging of this year’s edition.
“Congratulations to all parties involved in making it a success. May this momentum continue to elevate Malaysia’s name on the world motorsports stage,” he added.
The three-day Malaysian MotoGP, held at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from Oct 30-Nov 1, attracted about 196,000 visitors. — Bernama

Title: Melaka’s history of frequent chief minister changes should serve as a warning, says Adly Zahari
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 3 (Bernama) -- Melaka’s previous experience of seeing chief ministers replaced within a short period should serve as a lesson to all political parties to ensure the stability of the state administration is maintained after the 16th Melaka State Election, according to former Chief Minister Adly Zahari.
The Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman said political and administrative stability in the state should be a priority for all parties, rather than focusing solely on who would lead the state government after the election.
Adly, who is also Deputy Defence Minister and PH candidate for the Bukit Katil seat, said political stability must be taken seriously by all parties as it is an important ingredient in ensuring a stable administration that can sustain policies and development agendas.
“The issue is stability, not who wants to lead and so on. I think there are many ways we can use after the election. Whoever leads, our commitment is to ensure political stability,” he told Bernama.
Adly said one possible approach was the implementation of a Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA), similar to the one at the federal level, to ensure that the government has sufficient support to govern and pass the budget if it has only a slim majority.
Adly said an inclusive approach, including providing allocations to opposition state assemblymen, was among the measures he had implemented while serving as Chief Minister to ensure that all elected representatives could carry out their responsibilities to the community.
He said that when he led the state government, an allocation of RM60,000 was provided to each opposition state assemblyman to enable them to operate service centres and appoint staff to assist local residents.
He said the approach was important to ensure that elected representatives, regardless of whether they were from the government or opposition, had the means to serve the community while reducing political tensions.
Touching on his service in the Bukit Katil constituency, Adly said 231 of the 255 applications and complaints received from residents over the past two years had been resolved.
“Most involved infrastructure, drainage and drains. For schools, they requested speed bumps because vehicles were travelling too fast and endangering children on their way to school,” he said.
He said all applications received through various channels, including social media, the Information Department and elected representatives’ service centres, were recorded and forwarded to the relevant agencies for action and monitoring.
“Every time there is a meeting, I will look at the list of applications and ask whether they have been resolved. If they cannot be resolved, I will go down myself with the relevant agencies to see how the matter can be resolved,” he said.
Adly is facing a four-cornered contest against Perikatan Nasional candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif, Parti Bersama Malaysia candidate Dr Aliza Che Amran and independent candidate Abu Bakar Sabudin.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day, with early voting on Nov 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/ — Bernama

Title: TM Nxera says Iskandar Puteri data centre has required approvals, sustainability measures amid Johor residents’ concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — TM Nxera has said its data centre campus in Iskandar Puteri, Johor, is being developed on designated land with the necessary regulatory approvals, following media reports of residents’ concerns over power transmission infrastructure and data centre development in the area.
In a statement today, the company said the project complied with the conditions imposed by the relevant authorities.
“We take these concerns seriously. The TM Nxera campus is being developed on land designated for this purpose, with the requisite approvals from the relevant authorities, and in compliance with the conditions attached to them,” it said.
TM Nxera also said the campus had incorporated sustainability measures into its design and obtained provisional GreenRE Platinum certification.
The company clarified that it neither owned nor operated the power transmission infrastructure in the area.
However, it said it would continue working with relevant parties to help address concerns raised by the surrounding community.
“TM Nxera remains committed to supporting Malaysia’s digital economy, while being a responsible neighbour to the communities around us,” it added.
Earlier today Singapore’s
The Straits Times
reported that some homeowners in Iskandar Puteri were considering selling their properties over concerns about nearby data centre developments and high-voltage transmission towers, including a resident who put her RM1 million home in Eco Botanic up for sale following construction of TM Nxera’s 64-megawatt facility.
Residents in nearby Nusantara Prima and Nusa Bayu had also reportedly complained about construction dust, persistent humming noises and higher temperatures, which they believed were linked to data centre developments in the area.

Title: Cloud seeding carried out in peninsula, Sarawak to mitigate impact of transboundary haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — A total of 12 cloud seeding operations were carried out in several parts of Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak between Aug 30 and Oct 23 to mitigate the impact of transboundary haze on the country’s air quality.
The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) said the operations were conducted by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) in collaboration with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).
It said the operations covered the northern, central and southern regions of Peninsular Malaysia, as well as Sarawak, during the transboundary haze episode.
“The operations successfully induced rainfall in several targeted areas, helping to raise water levels in dams and reduce the impact of transboundary haze,” it said in a written reply published on the Parliament website.
The ministry was replying to a question from Datuk Larry Soon (PBM-Julau) on measures taken by the government to address transboundary haze caused by open burning in neighbouring country.
NRES said the government had also activated various preparedness measures, including the National Open Burning Action Plan and the National Haze Action Plan, to prevent and mitigate the effects of haze.
It said checks conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Plantation and Commodities had so far found no official information or evidence linking any Malaysian-related plantation companies to forest or plantation fires in Indonesia.
“Nevertheless, the government takes any allegations involving Malaysian-related companies seriously, and any information or evidence presented must be examined in cooperation with the relevant authorities, in accordance with applicable laws and jurisdictions,” the ministry said. — Bernama

Title: Melaka PH unveils manifesto with 12 pledges, targets 25 million visitors by 2032
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 3 — Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) has unveiled its ‘Melaka Rumah Kita’ manifesto, outlining three main thrusts and 12 aspirations aimed at improving public welfare, expanding economic opportunities and promoting clean, transparent and efficient governance.
Its chairman, Adly Zahari, said the first thrust focused on transforming Melaka into a smart state to improve efficiency, security and quality of life.
“Under the second thrust, PH proposes allocating 30 per cent of local authority contracts to young men and women to provide employment, business opportunities and practical experience for local youths.
“Under the third thrust, PH aims to attract 25 million visitors to Melaka by 2032, positioning the state as a more competitive, internationally recognised destination,” he said at a daily press conference and the launch of the manifesto at the PH main operations centre in Bukit Piatu here today.
Also present were Melaka PH deputy chairman Khoo Poay Tiong and acting Melaka PKR state leadership council chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim.
Adly said the manifesto’s 12 aspirations included affordable housing, people-friendly governance, quality employment, women’s empowerment, entrepreneurship and public welfare, improving traffic flow, strengthening Islamic institutions and religious activities, developing idle land for economic opportunities, optimising state land use and preserving social unity and harmony.
He said the manifesto was developed based on feedback gathered through engagements with residents and traders, alongside PH’s experience in state and federal administration.
“With these three thrusts and 12 aspirations, this ‘Melaka Rumah Kita’ manifesto sets out our direction for a government that upholds public trust, creates income opportunities and ensures development improves people’s lives.
“We hope these aspirations will be discussed and considered by the public. We will also introduce additional areas of focus to fulfil our commitment to serving the people, particularly by helping ease their cost-of-living burden.
“PH also plans to organise a series of forums and programmes to explain each of the proposed aspirations to voters throughout the campaign for the state election,” he said.
Early voting for the election is scheduled for Nov 10, with polling day set for Nov 14.
For the latest news on the state polls, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/ — Bernama

Title: Human Resources Ministry ready to assist Utusan Malaysia staff facing possible layoffs, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) is ready to assist media personnel and journalists affected by job layoffs through various forms of aid, including the Employment Insurance System (EIS) under the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso).
The Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said this while answering a question from Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai) regarding the allegation that between 100 and 200 Utusan Malaysia employees might lose their jobs due to management and financial problems believed to be faced by the media company.
He said that if the layoffs really happen, the ministry will apply and ask the involved companies to submit applications for assistance and review the eligibility of the affected workers under the EIS.
“EIS benefit applications can be made within 60 days from the date of job loss, provided that the specified contribution eligibility is met and relevant supporting documents are submitted,” he said during the oral question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said the ministry also provided several other intervention measures to help affected workers.
“I have prepared six steps that we will take and I will share them with the Yang Berhormat Pulai so that we can together see what role the ministry will play,” he also said.
Yesterday it was reported that Media Mulia, the publisher of Utusan Malaysia and Kosmo, would be restructuring its business to align operations with the shift of the media industry towards digital, affecting around 100 employees and journalists from both newspapers. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan land revenue rises RM60.36m to RM404m as state eyes RM1b target by 2030
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 3 — Negeri Sembilan’s land revenue collection increased by RM60.36 million to RM404.04 million as at Sept 30, compared with RM343.68 million recorded in the corresponding period last year.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the collection represented 98.10 per cent of the RM411.86 million target set for this year.
He said the achievement was also supported by non-tax revenue, which recorded collections of RM256.29 million against a target of RM245.62 million, while tax revenue collection amounted to RM147.74 million against a target of RM166.24 million.
“For state land tax collection, the amount recorded as at Sept 30 this year was RM144.18 million, compared with RM143.64 million in the corresponding period last year, representing a surplus of RM534,975.93.
“The state government hopes that the implementation of the e-Tanah System, particularly through the introduction of the Revenue Module and online services, will help it achieve its target of collecting RM1 billion in state revenue by 2030,” he told reporters after officiating the kick-off ceremony for the development of the Negeri Sembilan e-Tanah System here today.
He said the e-Tanah project, which involves a cost of RM185.4 million, represents a major investment by the state government in its efforts to modernise land administration and improve the efficiency of service delivery to the public.
Meanwhile, Ismail said the system’s implementation would also place emphasis on the accuracy and integrity of land ownership data, including efforts to resolve issues involving overlapping land titles, inaccurate information, land tax calculation errors and cancelled ownership records that still remain in the system.
He said system and data security must also be prioritised to address risks of fraud, forged titles and data manipulation that could undermine the interests of the state government and landowners.
Ismail said the system was expected to facilitate transactions for licensed land surveyors and housing developers, particularly in submitting land development applications online. It would also enable senior officers to monitor file movements and application statuses in real time.
He said the implementation of e-Tanah was also in line with the introduction of the Sixteenth Schedule to the National Land Code, which allows electronic land titles to be issued without the need to print physical documents, thereby reducing reliance on physical document storage.
“To ensure the project progresses according to plan, the vendor has also been asked to provide a dedicated dashboard to enable the management of the state Director of Lands and Mines Office to monitor development progress, the achievement of each phase, and any issues or delays requiring immediate attention,” he said.
He said all promised features and functions must be fully implemented to ensure the investment delivers measurable results while meeting the needs of land administration and the expectations of the public. — Bernama

Title: Anwar urges LHDN to balance technology with human judgement in tax administration
Article:
CYBERJAYA, Nov 3 — As of Nov 2, about 269,900 taxpayers submitted a total of 2.14 billion e-invoices, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said its implementation is not intended to introduce new taxes or increase the public’s tax burden.
On the contrary, e-invoices are an important instrument to uphold fairness, detect non-compliance and ensure that all parties fulfil their respective tax responsibilities, he said.
The use of the latest technology, data analytics and automation is important in strengthening tax administration. However, decisions must not be left entirely to technology without human consideration, particularly when people’s rights and interests are involved, he said.
“AI does not possess moral values or humanity. Technology has intelligence, but it cannot replace human wisdom, conscience and judgement,” he said in his speech at the 2026 Innovation and Integrity Day celebration today.
Anwar’s speech was delivered by Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan at the event organised by the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia (LHDN) today.
LHDN chief executive officer Datuk Dr Abu Tariq Jamaluddin and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar were also present.
Anwar said technological progress must always be guided by human values to ensure that its use benefits society.
He said it would be unfair if honest workers paid taxes from their earnings while those with greater financial resources concealed their income through multiple layers of business dealings and accounting tricks.
He therefore stressed that tax fairness required laws to be enforced equitably. LHDN officers must be firm against deliberate tax evasion while exercising discretion, within the framework of the law, towards taxpayers who require assistance and guidance, he said.
Anwar also said 2027 is expected to remain challenging amid global economic uncertainties.
“Prolonged conflicts in West Asia, supply disruptions and pressure on energy prices, and the risk of extreme weather conditions caused by the El Niño phenomenon could affect the cost of living and the well-being of the people.
“Therefore, the fifth Madani Budget 2027 mobilises RM510 billion in resources, including RM459.8 billion in federal government expenditure, to sustain development, strengthen economic resilience and safeguard the people’s welfare. Fair and effective revenue collection is essential to achieving these objectives,” he said.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation to all LHDN personnel for their contributions towards strengthening the country’s revenue position.
“Continue striving to master technology, improve efficiency and uphold integrity in carrying out every responsibility entrusted to you.
“However, amid technological advancements and revenue collection figures, never forget the people who form the foundation of every policy and action we take. Carry out your responsibilities not only with integrity, but also with compassion, wisdom and a deep appreciation of human values,” he stressed. — Bernama

Title: Daim family loses bid to stop police probe into alleged ‘government overthrow’ plot
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The High Court today reportedly struck out a lawsuit by the family of the late former finance minister Tun Daim Zainuddin and two lawyers seeking to halt a police investigation into an alleged plot to overthrow the government.
According to
Free Malaysia Today
, Justice Indra Nehru Savandiah allowed the government’s application to strike out the suit after finding that it disclosed no reasonable cause of action.
The judge reportedly found insufficient evidence to support the plaintiffs’ claim that the police investigation, conducted under Section 124B of the Penal Code, was carried out in bad faith.
She also found that allegations that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s public remarks had influenced the investigation were speculative and unsupported by facts, the report said.
The plaintiffs were Daim’s widow, Toh Puan Na’imah Abdul Khalid, their sons Amir and Amin, and lawyers Amir Zharif Abdullah and Nizamuddin Hamid, who had named Anwar, Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Mohd Khalid Ismail and the government as defendants.
The court reportedly made no order as to costs, while Indra said full grounds of judgment would be provided if an appeal was filed.
The plaintiffs were represented by Abraham Au and Gurdial Singh Nijar, while senior federal counsel Sallehuddin Ali and Solehheen Zaki appeared for the government, according to the report.
The investigation was launched following a police report lodged on February 26 alleging that an influential local figure had collaborated with international media organisations in an attempt to undermine the government.
Na’imah subsequently denied involvement in any attempt to overthrow the government, describing the allegations as false and claiming that the complainant was a disgruntled former employee.
On March 3, Anwar told Parliament that preliminary police investigations indicated that a group of Malaysians had worked with foreign parties to destabilise the government through international media and institutions.

Title: Anwar: Malaysia needs better tech to counter increasingly sophisticated drug smuggling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The increasingly sophisticated methods used in drug smuggling require more advanced detection technology at the country’s entry points to ensure that syndicate activities do not escape the attention of the authorities, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said reliance on existing scanning machines at airports was no longer sufficient as the technology was developed to detect weapons and explosives, rather than prohibited substances such as drugs concealed using more complex methods.
In this regard, he said new analytical facilities were being put in place to enhance drug detection capabilities.
“The facilities currently available are based on old technology, while smuggling methods have become more sophisticated and, at times, drugs concealed on the body cannot be detected. That is true.
“That is why new analytical facilities are now being provided to detect drugs, in addition to the K9 (Detection Dog Unit). Sometimes, the presence of these dogs also poses an issue for some passengers. This new facility has been acquired, but for now, it is only available at KLIA (Kuala Lumpur International Airport),” he said during the Ministers’ Question Time session in the Dewan Rakyat today. — Bernama

Title: PM: Expedite RM700m flood projects after repeated flooding in Sungai Buloh area
Article:
SUNGAI BULOH, Nov 3 —Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered work on the Sungai Buloh and Sungai Damansara flood mitigation projects to be expedited following repeated flooding in the area.
He said the two projects, costing nearly RM700 million and already approved by the federal government, must proceed without delay to minimise the risk of further flooding.
"Our priority is to speed things up. I have instructed that work such as river dredging, for which contracts have already been awarded, be expedited.
"What concerns me is that this area has been flooded two or three times. We need to widen the rivers, build additional retention ponds and carry out comprehensive flood mitigation measures," he told reporters after visiting the flood relief centre at the Siantan hall in Kampung Melayu Subang here today.
Anwar said he would obtain a progress report on the federal government's flood mitigation projects this Friday, while Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari is expected to present an update on state-level projects at the State Executive Council meeting on the same day. — Bernama

Title: Cheras custodial death probe: Family denies lawyers intimidated forensic specialist, demands focus on justice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — The younger brother of Noorizwan Zulkefly has rejected police allegations that the family’s legal team intimidated a hospital forensic specialist, calling on authorities to halt investigations against their lawyers and keep public scrutiny fixed on his brother’s custodial death.
In a media statement released today, Nooranis Zulkefly insisted that he attended the briefing in person and observed the forensic medicine consultant presenting and explaining his brother’s post-mortem photographs without any coercion, hostility, or pressure from their legal representatives.
“My wife, the three lawyers and two police officers from Bukit Aman were all present at the meeting with the forensic specialist doctor.
“During the meeting, the doctor voluntarily showed and explained the late Noorizwan’s post-mortem photographs,” he said.
The denial follows a police report lodged by the doctor, a government medical officer, which prompted Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to initiate a criminal probe against the family’s legal team under Sections 506, 186, and 189 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation, obstructing a public servant, and threatening a public servant.
CID director Datuk M. Kumar confirmed yesterday that investigators had recorded statements from the medical specialist and three legal practitioners linked to the case, while scheduling interviews with Noorizwan’s surviving kin.
Nooranis identified the three lawyers named in the probe as rights advocates N. Surendran, Latheefa Koya, and Dina Zamri.
Recounting the hospital briefing, Nooranis said he attended the consultation alongside his wife, the three lawyers, and two Bukit Aman police officers. He characterised the entire session as cordial and professional, noting that the family exchanged handshakes and posed for a commemorative photograph with the doctor before leaving.
Expressing bewilderment that harassment allegations were aired publicly despite two federal police officers witnessing the entire exchange, Nooranis questioned what factual foundation Bukit Aman possessed to accuse the lawyers of intimidation.
The dispute unfolds as Bukit Aman’s Prosecution and Legal Division (D5) prepares to submit the core custodial death investigation papers to the Attorney-General’s Chambers on Wednesday.
Investigators reclassified the death under Section 331 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort a confession, following clinical findings from Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz indicating that multiple external injuries across Noorizwan’s body were consistent with non-accidental blunt-force trauma, though the final autopsy analysis remains pending.
Nooranis today issued three primary demands from the family, insisting on an immediate cessation of “undue harassment” directed at their lawyers, full recognition of their counsel’s right to test evidence through due process without state interference, and a transparent prosecution of any custodial personnel implicated in his brother’s death.
Questioning why state scrutiny was turned against lawyers advocating for a grieving family rather than resolving a fatal custodial breach, Nooranis cautioned authorities against pursuing “baseless” diversions, concluding with the rally cry: “Do not divert the issue, do not harass our lawyers, justice for Noorizwan must be upheld”.

Title: Muhyiddin seeks to drop sedition charge over alleged Nenggiri campaign remarks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Former Prime Minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin will submit a representation to drop a charge of uttering seditious words during the 2024 Nenggiri state by-election campaign.
The sedition charge concerns his alleged claim that the Yang di-Pertuan Agong at the time did not invite him to be sworn in as Prime Minister after the 15th General Election, despite purportedly having the support of 115 of 222 MPs.
His lawyer, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, said the defence received a letter from the palace yesterday, after Muhyiddin was granted an audience by Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah.
“Without going into the details, Yang Arif, we wish to inform the court that our client was granted an audience by the palace on Oct 26. We have been made to understand that there are positive developments.
“Subsequently, yesterday, we were handed a letter from the palace. I will not go into the details, but based on that, Yang Arif, we would like to submit a fresh representation to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC),” he said during proceedings before High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin today.
“We do not wish to jeopardise whatever goodwill has been established by starting the trial, Yang Arif. So I think allow us this latitude, give us a bit of time. We will extend a copy of the letter directly to the AG for his consideration,” he added.
Deputy public prosecutor Azlina Rasdi did not object to the application.
The court then vacated all previously fixed trial dates and set Dec 3 for the parties to update the court on the representation.
On Aug 27, 2024, Muhyiddin, 79, who is also Bersatu president, was charged with uttering seditious words during the Nenggiri state by-election campaign at an open area near Dewan Semai Bakti Felda Perasu in Gua Musang, Kelantan, between 10.30 pm and 11.50 pm on Aug 14, 2024.
The charge was framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948 and is punishable under Subsection 4(1) of the same Act, which carries a maximum fine of RM5,000 or imprisonment of up to three years, or both, upon conviction.
The case was first mentioned at the Gua Musang Sessions Court in Kelantan on Aug 27, 2024, before it was transferred to the Kuala Lumpur High Court for trial following an application by the defence. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says he personally sympathises with Shuhaily, but stresses law and due process apply to everyone
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 3 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today defended Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail amid the controversy surrounding the police investigation into Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain over alleged assault.
Addressing questions in Parliament, Anwar expressed personal sympathy for the Malaysian Checkpoints and Borders Agency chief but said the rule of law must take its course without executive interference.
He said it was wrong to blame Saifuddin for the controversy amid calls for the minister to intervene, emphasising that authorities were obligated to investigate complaints against any officer regardless of their track record.
“Even a former Inspector-General of Police back in ‘98 was imprisoned for assaulting someone. Did he have contributions? Yes, he had contributions,” Anwar said, adding that professionalism and adherence to the law remained paramount.
The prime minister explained that the investigation into Shuhaily was initiated following a formal police report and reiterated that the government would not interfere in investigative or prosecutorial procedures.
“If there are allegations or accusations that someone was mistreated, it follows a process. Do not ask me or the home minister to interfere to that extent. Only now, if it is found by the prosecutors and the Attorney General that there is a case, charges will be brought,” he said.
Shuhaily, a former Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director, was charged at the Sepang Sessions Court in October 2026 with two counts of voluntarily causing hurt to two police officers under Section 323 of the Penal Code.
The charges stemmed from an alleged physical altercation involving Special Branch personnel stationed at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 on September 28, an incident that drew public attention after video footage circulated online.
The case has also attracted expressions of public support for Shuhaily on social media, with some commenters alleging that he was being victimised by rival factions within the police force.
Anwar said established civil service procedures applied when a public servant was formally charged, which could include reassignment or suspension pending legal proceedings, with such matters overseen by the Home Ministry.
Rejecting attempts to frame the investigation as a political controversy, Anwar urged the public and lawmakers not to confuse personal sympathy with legal immunity.
“If you ask me, I know him, I sympathise, and I know his track record,” he said.
“But I cannot say that just because a person is good, they can assault an officer. I cannot say that someone can bypass due legal process. Anger is one thing, but this is what I want to emphasise because there are attempts to confuse the matter.”

Title: Singapore teen among three fined RM3,500 under Malaysia’s new illegal racing law
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 3 — A 19-year-old Singaporean man was among three individuals fined RM3,500 each under the newly amended law against illegal racing by the Magistrate’s Court here today.
The three, Syajahan Alfian Abdullah, 19; Muhammad Daniel Hakim Mohamad Rashid, 24; and Gonzales Mckhovic anak George, 18, pleaded guilty to engaging in illegal racing and riding their motorcycles in a dangerous manner on the Second Link Expressway last month.
They entered their guilty pleas after the charges were read out to them individually before Magistrate Nur Fatin Mohamad Farid.
The court also ordered all three to serve four months in prison if they failed to pay their fines.
According to the charge sheet, Singaporean national serviceman Syajahan Alfian was accused of riding a motorcycle at high speed and participating in a speed contest at Kilometre 12.5 of the southbound section of the Second Link Expressway at 2.10am on October 18.
He was charged under Section 42A(2) of the Road Transport Act 1987, as amended in 2026, which carries a fine of between RM2,000 and RM10,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
Meanwhile, Muhammad Daniel Hakim and Gonzales Mckhovic were each charged with racing their motorcycles on the northbound section of the Second Link Expressway between Kilometres 7.8 and 18.2 at 2.10am on October 18.
Both men were charged under Section 42A(1) of the same Act, which carries a fine of between RM2,000 and RM10,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both.
The case was prosecuted by traffic police prosecuting officer Inspector S. Vikineswary, while all three accused were unrepresented.
The Road Transport (Amendment) Act 2026, which came into effect on October 16, introduced harsher penalties for illegal racing and reckless motorcycle riding through the inclusion of Section 42A.
The Transport Ministry said the amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333) were intended to enhance road safety, strengthen enforcement and modernise service delivery by the Road Transport Department (JPJ).
The amendments also aim to close legal loopholes that could allow certain parties to evade responsibility for offences committed using their vehicles.
